note: m0100-m0001 window agent, 2 Nov 2026. Fixes: Kanva land beyond Central India dropped when the dynasty ends (events/0); Rome's reversed Greek-cities vassalage closed (events/1); Gallia Narbonensis restored from the start of the window (events/2) and kept through the Roman keyframes -91, -87, -77, -66, -63; Asia kept Roman to 88 and Pontic until 85 (-91, -87); Gaul no longer Roman from 63 (-63); Germania an occupation from 12 BC, not plain Roman land from 14 BC (roman-empire -14). [Review 2 Nov 2026: the Province union in the five Roman keyframe overrides now leaves out Massalia's colonies at Nice and Agde; events/1's note brought up to date (a no-op guard since m0300-m0201 closes the 272 relation).]

region.text: the Kanva realm of the Ganges plain (Pataliputra to Panchala and Vatsa), without the Central Indian land (Vidisha) that the Satavahanas took

events.note: 28 BCE: the Satavahanas end the Kanva dynasty, but only in Central India. 'According to the Puranas, their dynasty was brought to an end by the Satavahanas in 28 BCE'; 'The defeat of the Kanva dynasty by the Satavahana dynasty was a localised event in Central India'; 'After the defeat at the hands of Satavahanas and the fall of the Kanva dynasty, the Magadha empire came to an end'; 'Magadha later came under the hegemony of the Mitra dynasty of Kaushambi from the 1st century BCE'. The page names no Satavahana rule over the Ganges plain, yet the Kanva dissolve hands all of the realm's remaining land to the Satavahanas (succession), and the -27 keyframe then strips 3,000 cells of it again: this loss to nobody drops the Ganges-plain land when the dynasty ends, so only the Central Indian land that the Satavahana gain names passes on.

Rome, not the Italiot Greek cities, was the stronger party from 272 BC: 'The remaining resistance to Rome among the Italiot Greeks collapsed, with the remaining cities quickly seeking terms' and 'Its victory over the peninsular Greeks also cemented Rome's hegemony over Italy'. A guard: it closes the 272 Rome-Greek cities vassal relation if it is still open, which the compiler had read with the roles reversed (Rome the Greek cities' vassal, Rome's land in their tint). [Review 2 Nov 2026: m0300-m0201 events/0 and events/1 now close that relation in 272 itself, so in the trial this entry closes nothing; harmless.]

region.text: Gallia Transalpina, the province of 121 BC from the Pyrenees and Cévennes to the Alps and the Gulf of Lion, less Massilia's own territory

events.note: Gallia Transalpina is Roman from 121 BC ('The area became a Roman province in 121 BC'; Narbo Martius 'founded on the coast in 118 BC'), but at 1 January 100 BC Rome holds only a coastal strip of it: the 121 BC gain (/ledger/122) was released by an earlier keyframe snap to a Cliopatria shape that draws only the coast. Restored here, and carried through the 91, 87, 77, 66 and 63 keyframes by their overrides. If the m0200-m0101 patch already restores it this changes nothing.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 91 shape without the land the Italian confederation held from late 91, with Gallia Transalpina; Asia stays Roman until early 88, when the ledger (/ledger/140) takes it

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's correction also cut Mysia, Troad, Lydia, Ionia and Caria from 91, but Asia fell only in 88: 'This swift conquest of Asia through Phrygia took place in early 88' (First Mithridatic War page), and the ledger already removes it in 88. The cut stayed hidden only because the reversed Greek-cities tint kept Rome's cells out of the snap; with that closed, the keyframe would strip Asia three years early. Gallia Narbonensis: 'The area became a Roman province in 121 BC', bordered by 'the Pyrenees Mountains on the west, the Cévennes to the north, the Alps on the east, and the Gulf of Lion on the south'; Cliopatria's Roman shapes draw only a coastal strip of it, so the land the ledger gave Rome in 121 (/ledger/122) is released at the first snap. [Review 2 Nov 2026: Massalia's colonies Nikaia (Nice) and Agathe (Agde) cut from the Province: with them in the union the 87 snap gave both Massaliot cells to Rome by R2 (Rome succeeds Massalia), 38 years early. Massalia page: the city founded 'colonies of its own on the sea coast of Gallia Narbonensis', among them 'Agathe' and 'Nikaia'; Gallia Narbonensis page: only 'After the war ended in Caesar's favour, Massilia lost all of its independence' (49 BC).]

The dossier's correction added Mysia, Troad, Lydia, Ionia and Caria to the 87 shape 'from 85', but a keyframe acts from its first year, so Rome held Asia in 87 and 86 while Mithridates did: 'The treaty of Dardanos was in effect a return to the status quo of 89' (late summer or early autumn 85), and Sulla in 86 still demanded that Mithridates 'surrender all his conquests'. The ledger already returns Asia and Phrygia in 85 (/ledger/146), so Cliopatria's 87 shape as drawn is right. Gallia Narbonensis: 'The area became a Roman province in 121 BC', bordered by 'the Pyrenees Mountains on the west, the Cévennes to the north, the Alps on the east, and the Gulf of Lion on the south'; Cliopatria's Roman shapes draw only a coastal strip of it, so the land the ledger gave Rome in 121 (/ledger/122) is released at the first snap.
